market_context: United States; bone-in Spanish Serrano ham kept at home
title: How to store a whole Spanish ham after you start cutting it

seo.title: How to store a whole Spanish ham after you start cutting it
seo.meta_description: Keep a started bone-in Serrano ham cool, dry, ventilated and away from light, and protect the cut face from drying. Boneless centers and sliced ham should be refrigerated instead.
seo.search_intent: Explain how to store a started bone-in Spanish ham and how that differs from opened boneless or sliced ham.

excerpt: A started bone-in Serrano ham should be kept in a cool, dry, ventilated place with little light, while the exposed cut face is protected with clean pieces of the ham's own fat and a clean cloth. The Spanish Serrano consortium gives 12–20°C (54–68°F) for whole pieces. Open boneless centers and sliced ham belong in the refrigerator.
content_html:
Once you make the first cut into a whole dry-cured ham, you create a surface that was previously protected. That face can lose moisture and oxidize, so good storage is mainly about protecting the cut while keeping the whole ham in the right environment.

Keep a bone-in ham cool, dry and ventilated

The Consorcio del Jamón Serrano Español recommends storing whole Serrano ham in a dry, clean, ventilated place at about 12–20°C (54–68°F) with as little light as practical.

A hot kitchen beside the oven or a sunny window is therefore a poor location. If your home routinely runs warmer than that range, choose the coolest appropriate space available and follow the producer's specific instructions.

Cover the freshly cut face

When opening the ham, save a few clean pieces of the outer fat. The consortium recommends laying some of that fat over the exposed meat to slow surface drying, then covering the whole piece with a clean cloth.

The goal is protection, not sealing the entire bone-in ham into a humid airtight environment.

Do not strip the whole ham at once

Remove rind and outer fat only from the area you are about to slice. Leaving the rest of the natural covering intact protects a much larger part of the ham from unnecessary air exposure.

Boneless and sliced ham are different

An opened boneless center or package of slices does not have the same protective structure. The Serrano consortium recommends refrigeration at 2–10°C (36–50°F) for boneless centers and sliced portions, with exposed surfaces protected in food-safe wrapping.

For commercially packed Spanish ham sold in the U.S., the label's storage instructions take priority, especially after opening.

What if the surface darkens?

A thin dried or darker layer can develop where the ham meets air. That is often oxidation and moisture loss rather than proof that the entire piece is spoiled. Slice away the dried surface until the aroma and texture are normal again.

The useful distinction

Bone-in whole ham: cool, dry, ventilated and protect the cut face. Boneless or sliced ham: refrigerate and wrap appropriately. The package format determines the storage method.

faq.question: Does a started whole Serrano ham need refrigeration?
faq.answer: A traditional bone-in piece can be stored cool, dry and ventilated; the Spanish Serrano consortium recommends 12–20°C (54–68°F). Follow the producer label if it says otherwise.

faq.question: What should cover the cut face?
faq.answer: Clean pieces of the ham's own outer fat can be placed over the exposed meat, with a clean cloth over the piece.

faq.question: Should sliced Serrano ham be refrigerated?
faq.answer: Yes. Open sliced and boneless formats should be refrigerated according to package instructions.
